$comment: The lint warnings this repository currently tolerates, each with its reason.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (3b, 2026-08-18). Standing reports had been calling the
lint warnings 'allowlisted' for several sessions. An external audit went
looking for the allowlist and there wasn't one: the warnings were merely
TOLERATED, and the word in the reports described a mechanism that did not
exist. A count nobody can check is a count that drifts, and 'allowlisted'
was doing the work of 'we looked at these and they're fine' without anybody
having looked.
So the word now has a mechanism behind it. `corepack pnpm lint:allowlist`
runs ESLint, matches every warning against the entries below, and REFUSES
when a warning appears that is not listed here. It also names entries that
no longer match anything, because a stale allowlist quietly grows into
permission for whatever comes next.
MATCHING IS ON file + rule + symbol, DELIBERATELY NOT ON LINE NUMBER.
A line number drifts every time somebody edits above it, and an allowlist
that goes stale on an unrelated edit is one people learn to regenerate
without reading — which is the same as not having one.
AN ENTRY HERE IS NOT AN ENDORSEMENT. Every current entry is an unused
symbol, and most are dead references that should simply be deleted. They
are recorded rather than fixed because deleting code is not this session's
brief; the file states what each one is so the next person can act on it
instead of rediscovering it.
THE `^_` DISCARDS LEFT THIS FILE (g18, 2026-08-18, the author's ruling A).
Fifteen entries became twelve. The three removed - _whichVote, _ok and _d -
were deliberate discards, and a deliberate discard is not a warning we
tolerated; it is not a warning. eslint.config.mjs now carries the `^_`
convention, so they are legal at the linter rather than excused here.
The ruling named varsIgnorePattern; all three are PARAMETERS, so
argsIgnorePattern is what reaches them. Both are set and the difference is
recorded in the config, not smoothed over.
